transcriptText:
Same hand, two sizes. Which one does the job? Kings, on jack, eight, three, deuce... and two hearts are out there. The pot's 120. You want to stop a flush draw calling cheaply. 40, or 90?

Bet a third of the pot. If he calls, his call is 1/5 of the final pot... that's his price. A bluff that size needs a fold 1 time in 4. Half pot... a quarter, and a third. The full pot... a third, and a half. Every size moves both.

Now sit in his seat, holding two hearts. 9 more are left, of 46 cards he can't see... 19.6%. Facing 40, his price is 40 of 200. 20%... close to fair. Facing 90, it's 90 of 300. 30%... now he loses about 31 chips a call. Bigger works here because of his price... not because bigger wins more.

Your turn. A river where you want his weaker pairs to call. A third... 1/5, and a quarter. Three-quarters... 3/10, and 3/7. To keep those pairs calling, bet the third. So pick the size from the job. Charge draws, invite worse hands, or make folds cheap to win. Up next: value betting.
